text:
Maria (Support): Hey team, P0 from a paying customer — multiple 502/504s hitting hosted inference endpoints for a subset of orgs since ~09:12 UTC. They report intermittent failures on generate calls, spikes in latency prior, then 502s. Customer trace ids: req-0a1b2c3d, req-4e5f6g7h. Escalating because it's affecting production workflows.
Sam (Eng-SRE): copy. any pattern on backend? region/route/model? or only certain tenants?
Maria (Support): Only hosted-api (us-east-1) and seems correlated to calls that include the org billing header x-customer-account. Not every request, but high error rate when traffic bursts from those tenants.
Josh QA: I pulled a few edge logs for one tenant — envoy shows upstream reset + 502. snippet:
```
[envoy] [2026-03-15T09:13:02Z] cluster upstream reset: reason="upstream connection termination" upstream_host="10.12.45.67:8080" response_code=502 x-request-id=req-0a1b2c3d
```
Maria (Support): customer also sent curl repro:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "x-customer-account: 12345" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
# returns HTTP/2 502 or sometimes hangs then 504
```
Ryan (Oncall): Any recent deploys to auth or edge in the last hour? Could be a change that interacts poorly with keepalives/HTTP2.
deploy-bot: Deploy completed: edge-proxy v3.12.0 at 2026-03-15T08:58:10Z; artifact: edge-proxy@3.12.0; rollout 100%.
Sam (Eng-SRE): ok, edge-proxy 3.12.0 rolled. What changed in 3.12.0? Alex, you or someone on Edge team?
Alex (Edge): 3.12.0 enabled h2 connection pooling optimizations and aggressive connection reuse to upstreams (to reduce TLS handshakes). We also tweaked max_concurrent_streams handshake hint. Haven't seen issues in canary but maybe interplay with auth service which is older.
Josh QA: Reproduced locally with load test hitting auth-backed routes: saw stream reset errors and auth returned 502 downstream when stream limit hit. Log from auth:
```
[auth] ERROR: accept failed: unexpected EOF on keepalive
[auth] WARN: connection closed while reading headers
```
Sam (Eng-SRE): hypothesis: edge now uses persistent HTTP/2 multiplexing to upstream auth which keeps long-lived streams; if auth doesn't handle that well it may drop/reset TCP leading Envoy to surface 502/504. Could also be h2 stream id exhaustion or framing issue.
Maria (Support): Customer impact: high for ~5% of requests from those tenants, some retries succeed. They want ETA + mitigations.
Ryan (Oncall): Immediate mitigations we can try:
- roll edge-proxy back to previous version (quickest)
- enforce edge->upstream as HTTP/1.1 (disable h2 for auth route) to avoid multiplexing
- increase keepalive/stream limits on auth in a quick config patch
Which is easiest?
Alex (Edge): I can push a config to disable h2->upstream for the auth service in ~10m (route-level change). Rollback needs org approval but is doable.
Sam (Eng-SRE): I can instrument additional debug logs on envoy (upstream stream resets) and collect full traces for the provided request ids. Maria, please ask customer for a few more sample request timestamps + request bodies if allowed.
Maria (Support): pinged customer for 10 mins of logs and said we're on it. Provided them ETA: 30-45m for a mitigation and will follow up.
Josh QA: repro steps for SRE to run locally:
1) spin up auth service v1.7 (http/1.1 only) and v1.8 (has flaky h2 handling)
2) run wrk2 against edge-proxy with 500 concurrent, header x-customer-account set
3) watch envoy logs for "upstream reset" and auth logs for EOF
I can drop the exact wrk command in the thread.
Ryan (Oncall): do it. Also let's prepare rollback plan if config patch doesn't help in 15m.
Alex (Edge): rolling config now to disable h2 to auth cluster. I'll post once completed.
Alex (Edge): config change applied at 09:29 UTC — edge->auth is now forced to HTTP/1.1 for that cluster. Monitoring...
Sam (Eng-SRE): watching spike dashboard. Errors dropped from ~7% -> ~1.2% in 3m. Latency improved. Looks promising.
Maria (Support): Customer confirmed improvement on their end :) they're still seeing rare 502s during big bursts but much better. They've asked for root cause and prevention.
Josh QA: writeup idea: rollout of h2 pooling + older auth not handling long-lived multiplexed streams -> connection resets under burst -> envoy surfaces 502/504. Recommended long-term: upgrade auth to h2-compliant stack or maintain per-route protocol compatibility checks. Short-term: keep HTTP/1.1 forced for auth cluster until upgrade.
Ryan (Oncall): agree. I'll create an incident follow-up: collect more traces, timeline, capture pcap for one repro, check kernel-level resets on auth hosts, and schedule auth upgrade with product.
Maria (Support): closing loop with customer, offering postmortem and timeline. Thanks everyone. :heart:
deploy-bot: Incident annotated: edge-proxy rollback not performed; config patch forced protocol changes. Tagging for postmortem.
Sam (Eng-SRE): I'll start the postmortem doc and add expected action items (edge config gating, canary with auth compatibility test, runtime protocol fallback).
